Authorised, lawful and proper use of NDIA ICT
Authorised use of NDIA ICT
Use NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications and information resources only for authorised NDIA purposes and in accordance with legal, policy and APS obligations.

Users must use NDIA ICT for authorised NDIA work. Limited personal use is permitted only when it is lawful, reasonable, low risk, does not interfere with work, and complies with NDIA policies, lawful directions and applicable laws.
Mandatory
High

APS-VCE-02: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(4)-(5); APSC Code of Conduct elements.
APS-EPC-01: Public Service Act 1999 ss 10, 10A and 13; APSC APS Values guidance.

PSA-02: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(8).

Respectful, lawful and inclusive digital conduct
Prevent discrimination, bullying, harassment, abuse, hate speech, victimisation, adverse action and offensive conduct through NDIA digital channels.

Users must not use NDIA ICT, email, messaging, meetings, collaboration tools or social media to discriminate, bully, harass, threaten, intimidate, humiliate, abuse, victimise, sexually harass, coerce, or publish hateful, hostile or offensive material.

Data analytics, AI and automated decision support
Control bias, protected-attribute profiling, accuracy and transparency risks in analytics, automated decisions and decision-support outputs.

Users must not use NDIA data, analytics, AI tools, profiling or decision-support outputs to make or support decisions based on irrelevant protected attributes, stereotypes or biased assumptions. Outputs that may affect a person must be accurate, reviewed, transparent where required and approved for use.

Records, retention, disposal, legal holds and FOI
Capture official business information in approved systems, preserve records for accountability and use authorised retention, disposal and release processes.

Users must store official NDIA business information in approved systems and must not delete, alter, destroy, move, conceal, retain only locally, or dispose of NDIA records unless authorised. Records relevant to FOI, legal, audit, complaint, investigation or parliamentary processes must be preserved and released only through approved channels.
